item.title: Carolina Concha Ramírez
item.description: Trained as an environmental chemist, she has been a Ph.D. student in Social Complexity Sciences since 2025. She currently works in experimental social science, with an interest in the study of the environment and the interactions between the environment, natural resources and society. Her research focuses on the sustainability of common-pool resources and on how certain kinds of information and different communication mechanisms can help integrate ecological dynamics into decision-making processes.

item.title: Juan Illanes
item.description: Physicist from the Universidad de Concepción and Ph.D. student in Social Complexity Sciences at the Universidad del Desarrollo, a program he joined in 2025. His academic path focuses on studying economic phenomena through quantitative and computational approaches, integrating tools from physics, data science and the social sciences. His current research focuses on the relationship between financial news and the dynamics of commodity markets. In particular, he studies how the sentiment expressed in news coverage relates to returns and volatility, using language analysis and BERT-based machine learning models.

item.title: Alejandra Molina
item.description: Alejandra Molina is a Professor at the School of Government of Universidad del Desarrollo. She holds a Ph.D. in Social Complexity Sciences from Universidad del Desarrollo. She also holds an M.Sc. in Meteorology and Climatology and bachelor’s degrees in Geophysics and in Astronomy from the Universidad de Chile. Her career bridges the physical and the social sciences. Between 2010 and 2021 she studied solar radiation at the Universidad de Chile. She developed radiative transfer models and nationwide databases from satellite information.

item.title: Aníbal Olivera
item.description: Aníbal Olivera is a Ph.D. student in Social Complexity Sciences, funded by an ANID National Doctoral Scholarship. He previously trained in Physics at the Universidad de Concepción, where he earned a B.Sc. in Physics and an M.Sc. in Physics. His research studies how the structure of social networks shapes the diffusion and abandonment of behaviors. In Networks Decide for Us he imputes homophilous networks onto representative surveys to measure how much of diffusion is due to topology; in Network Disadoption he proposes a measure of exposure to neighbors who abandon a behavior; and in Political Networks he analyzes collaboration among members of Chile’s 2021-2022 Constitutional Convention.

item.title: Denise Laroze
item.description: Denise Laroze is an Associate Professor at the Research Center for Social Complexity (CICS) of the School of Government at Universidad del Desarrollo. She holds a Ph.D. in Government (Political Science) from the University of Essex and an M.Sc. in Political Science and Political Economy from the London School of Economics, United Kingdom. She currently leads the Mobile Experimental Laboratory within the PoliCICS group. Her academic research specializes in behavioral science and decision-making.

item.title: Francisco Villarroel
item.description: Francisco Villarroel-Riquelme is a Ph.D. student in Social Complexity Sciences at the Research Center for Social Complexity (CICS) at Universidad del Desarrollo, Chile. His doctoral dissertation currently focuses on leadership, social norms, and antisocial behavior. He worked as a research assistant at the Center for Experimental Social Sciences at the University of Santiago, Chile, and as an assistant researcher in several publicly funded research projects. These projects addressed Foucault’s theory of governmentality, social networks and their consequences in social life, safe sex behaviors in undergraduate students, and behavioral web designs on pension systems.

item.title: Jorge Fábrega
item.description: Jorge Fábrega is an Associate Professor and researcher at the Research Center for Social Complexity (CICS) of the School of Government at Universidad del Desarrollo. He holds degrees in Business and Economics (1996) and in Sociology (1998) from the Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile, and earned his Ph.D. in Public Policy from the University of Chicago in 2009. From 2018 to 2022 he directed the Ph.D. Program in Social Complexity Sciences at Universidad del Desarrollo, where he currently teaches Political Economy and Social Network Theory.
